extracted.intended_audience: aspiring novelists preparing a one-page synopsis for agents or writing-course submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing a concise, one-page synopsis of a novel to include in a pitch package sent to agents or for novel-writing courses. Focuses on what to include, how to present plot and character, tone, length and special-case advice for experimental works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put your title at the top
rubrics_metrics.description: Put your title at the top
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if it’s still just a working title.

rubrics_metrics.name: State the genre
rubrics_metrics.description: State what genre you’re writing in
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you're writing genre fiction (eg romance, science fiction, fantasy, crime thriller, psychological suspense) indicate it. If you’re not writing in a clear genre or you’re not sure what your genre is, just skip this. If you’re writing for children, indicate the age group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfect your pitch line (key question/dilemma/heart)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include your pitch line at or near the top — usually the key question, dilemma or driving force of the novel (the heart of the novel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a great hook or a high concept, that should be your pitch line. Don’t over-fret: you will expand on the story below the line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a quote only if it helps (quote or pitch line, not both)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some people like to include a quote from the novel to offer a glimpse of the tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A quote can be a good option if you’re struggling with a pitch line. Pick one approach — you don’t need both a quote and a pitch line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep it simple — cover plot in broad strokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Set out your story in the simplest terms; cover the plot in broad strokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t try to include everything — we don’t need intricate twists, turns and subplots, just the major plot points so an agent can see what your novel is and where it’s headed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show the protagonist and motivations early
rubrics_metrics.description: Get your protagonist’s name in early on (if you have one clear protagonist) and state the main character's motivations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It’s good to show whose story this is. But don’t put in too many character names — a full cast list will clutter and confuse the synopsis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set the scene: primary setting and time period
rubrics_metrics.description: Give us the when and the where: the primary setting for the novel and the time period in which it takes place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly important for historical fiction. The default is to assume ‘now’. Don’t include lots of place names and dates — keep it simple.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide whether to include the ending (spoiler policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to include the ending of the novel is optional and agents differ in preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some agents say they need to see the ending; others dislike big twists being given away. You can’t realistically rewrite your synopsis for every agent, so decide what feels right for you and your novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey the tone as well as the plot
rubrics_metrics.description: The best synopses convey the tone of the novel as well as the plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you can bring the feel, atmosphere or voice of the novel into the synopsis it will bring it to life — optional but adds extra zing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid self-praise
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t heap praise on your own novel in the synopsis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is not the place to say you’re going to be a huge international bestseller or to label the work gripping/funny/moving — leave judgments to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be succinct — one page (~500 words), readable formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: One page should be enough to cover the necessary information (approx. 500 words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to be succinct and don’t try to wedge in more words by shrinking font, spacing or margins — that makes the synopsis difficult to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t share your full plan or chapter breakdowns
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include chapter breakdowns or mini-summaries of the content of individual bits of your book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This isn’t your working plan — the agent or publisher doesn’t need to see that level of detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise story over listing themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Go for story rather than ‘themes’. Tell us what drives your novel rather than giving a list of themes or imagery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only mention themes if your book explores a big issue or if a theme (eg grief) is the major driving force of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t flag an unreliable narrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t point out that your first-person narrator is unreliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calling attention to unreliability is unnecessary — essentially every first-person narrator is unreliable; it’s a redundant note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling unusual or experimental narrative structures
rubrics_metrics.description: If your novel is so experimental that it resists a normal synopsis, try to write a page that gives an idea of what you’re trying to do or a page from a character’s perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the experimental synopsis reads like an academic exercise or is pretentious and unreadable, don’t send it — instead send the pitch letter and opening. Note that most novels can be synopsised normally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a synopsis in your pitch package
rubrics_metrics.description: The synopsis sits alongside the opening of your novel and your agent pitch letter in your pitch package and lays out the complete narrative arc of your plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some agents will read the synopsis before the writing sample; others will check it after; some barely glance. Nonetheless you should write a good one-page synopsis when ready to send your novel out.
